title: Module 11 Vocabulary Check
intro: Answer each item. Feedback comes right away. Items you miss come back for a retry round.

items.q: A factor in a factorial design is
o: An independent variable with two or more levels
items.why: In a 2 by 3 design there are two factors, one with two levels and one with three.

items.q: A 2 by 2 design has how many cells?
items.why: Multiply the number of levels of each factor.

o: The overall effect of one factor, averaging across the levels of the other
The effect of both factors together
The difference within a single cell
items.why: It is evaluated using the marginal means.

o: The effect of one factor depends on the level of the other factor
The groups are the same size
items.why: It is a difference in differences. Parallel lines in an interaction plot mean no interaction.

items.q: On a plot of cell means, non-parallel lines suggest
o: A significant main effect of both factors
items.why: Whether the departure from parallel is larger than chance is tested by the interaction F.

items.q: A two-factor ANOVA produces how many F ratios?
o: Three: factor A, factor B, and the interaction
items.why: Each of the two main effects and the interaction gets its own F, all using MS within as the denominator.

items.q: SS total in a two-factor ANOVA equals
o: SS A plus SS B plus SS AxB plus SS within
items.why: The total variability is partitioned into four parts.

items.q: Degrees of freedom for the AxB interaction in a 2 by 2 design are
items.why: df AxB = (levels of A minus 1) times (levels of B minus 1) = 1 times 1.

o: The means for each level of one factor, averaged over the other factor

items.q: A factorial design has an advantage over two separate one-factor studies because it
o: Tests how factors combine, which separate studies cannot
items.why: Only a factorial design can reveal whether one factor's effect depends on another.
